title: Apply secure coding guidelines and standards
question: As untrusted text crosses API, object-authorization, database, and browser-interpreter boundaries, which distinct control answers each question?
scenario: A search API concatenates a query string and returns detailed error messages.
focalRelation: untrusted input --server-side type/length/business validation--> application authenticated subject plus object/action --server-side authorization--> data request parameters --separate data from query structure--> database stored text --context-specific output encoding--> browser interpreter safe errors/logs --exclude secrets while preserving correlation--> evidence request shape --input validation--> accepted data subject/object/action --authorization distinct from authentication--> access decision parameterized query --prevents data becoming query structure--> database returned data --context encoding and minimization--> client legacy exception --owner/compensating control/expiry/retest--> temporary state

nodes.label: Untrusted search input
nodes.detail: Caller-controlled query text, filters, object IDs, and rendering values.

nodes.label: API validation boundary
nodes.detail: Constrains type, length, syntax, allowed operations, authentication, authorization, and rate before data access.

nodes.label: Parameterized query
nodes.detail: Separates SQL code from data values so input cannot alter query structure.

nodes.label: Authorized record set
nodes.detail: Database result restricted by server-side object/action policy and minimum necessary fields.

nodes.label: Safe response and context encoder
nodes.detail: Maps internal failure to a bounded client error and encodes returned values for the exact HTML, attribute, URL, or script context.

nodes.label: Browser interpreter
nodes.detail: Consumes the rendered context; only context-encoded, minimized output may cross this boundary.

edges.label: crosses syntax, size, policy, and rate checks
binds validated values separately from SQL code
routes database failure to a non-sensitive client response
passes returned values through the exact output-context encoder

lanes.label: Untrusted input
lanes.rule: Client text and identifiers remain untrusted even after authentication.

lanes.label: API security boundary
lanes.rule: Validation, authorization, and rate controls run before data access.

lanes.label: Database boundary
lanes.rule: Parameterized operations and row/object policy protect query and results.

lanes.label: Safe response boundary
lanes.rule: Errors and output reveal only intended information.

lanes.label: Security evidence
lanes.rule: Logs retain useful context without credentials or sensitive payloads.

statuses.n2: server boundary must parse and authorize

states.title: Separate data from SQL structure
states.caption: Validation constrains the request, and parameter binding keeps caller text out of SQL command structure.

states.title: Reject the concatenated path
states.caption: Concatenation lets caller text become SQL structure. Returning the database error then exposes internal details without repairing the query.

states.title: Encode at the output boundary
states.caption: Authorized records remain untrusted for rendering. Encode each returned value for its exact browser context before it reaches the interpreter.

states.title: Keep the claims separate
states.caption: Parameterized SQL protects query structure; object authorization protects records; context encoding protects the browser boundary; safe errors reveal no internal detail.

statuses.n5: safe error and exact-context encoding verified

variants.label: Temporary encoding exception

prediction.prompt: The search API concatenates caller text into SQL and returns the database error. Which paired repair addresses the two interpreter boundaries?

options.label: HTML-encode the search text before concatenating it into SQL and keep the detailed error for support
options.feedback: HTML encoding does not separate SQL code from data, and a detailed database error exposes internal behavior.

options.label: Bind the search value as data and return a bounded client error while logging safe diagnostic context
options.feedback: Correct. Parameter binding protects SQL structure, while safe error handling prevents database internals from crossing the response boundary.

options.label: Hide the search route from navigation and rely on the framework to reject malicious queries
options.feedback: Route obscurity and framework defaults do not replace parameter binding, bounded input rules, safe errors, and negative tests.

prediction.hint: Name the control required at the database interpreter and the separate control required at the client-response boundary.

transfer.prompt: An API authenticates users but accepts any object ID supplied by the caller.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: An API authenticates users but accepts any object ID supplied by the caller. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Use parameterized queries, validate and constrain inputs, encode outputs for their rendering context, return safe errors, enforce object-level authorization, rate-limit, log security-relevant events without secrets, and test negative and abuse cases. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Add server-side object authorization and tests for horizontal and vertical privilege escalation. Authentication alone does not authorize access to every object.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: An API authenticates users but accepts any object ID supplied by the caller. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Use parameterized queries, validate and constrain inputs, encode outputs for their rendering context, return safe errors, enforce object-level authorization, rate-limit, log security-relevant events without secrets, and test negative and abuse cases. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

options.label: Add server-side object authorization and tests for horizontal and vertical privilege escalation
options.feedback: Correct. Add server-side object authorization and tests for horizontal and vertical privilege escalation. Authentication alone does not authorize access to every object.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A parameterized search result is safely queried, but a result name is inserted into an administrator page without HTML-context encoding. What control is missing?

options.label: Apply context-specific output encoding at rendering and test stored and reflected script payloads
options.feedback: Correct. Parameterization protects query structure; it does not make returned text safe for an HTML interpreter.

options.label: Rely on parameterized SQL because data that cannot inject SQL cannot inject browser content
options.feedback: The same data crosses a different interpreter with different control rules.

options.label: Delete angle brackets from every stored name and treat all rendering contexts as equivalent
options.feedback: Ad hoc filtering is brittle and ignores attribute, URL, script, and other output contexts.

retry.hint: The database interpreter and browser interpreter are separate trust boundaries.

takeaway: Use parameterized queries, validate and constrain inputs, encode outputs for their rendering context, return safe errors, enforce object-level authorization, rate-limit, log security-relevant events without secrets, and test negative and abuse cases.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implements the shared request-to-data treatment across concrete cases: the base separates caller data from SQL structure, safe client errors from internal failures, and returned data from the browser through an explicit context-encoder→browser-interpreter relation; the object-authorization variant stops cross-customer reads before retrieval; the exception-lifecycle variant names owner, exact scope, expiry, compensating control, permanent remediation, equivalent-path retest, evidence, and closure.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Validation, parameterized queries, server-side object authorization, contextual output encoding, and safe errors solve different boundary problems. Applying one control at the wrong interpreter or policy boundary leaves the other weakness intact.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: The authored boundary walkthrough keeps SQL structure, object policy, browser interpretation, and error handling distinct, enabling the learner to choose the control at the right boundary.
